# Schemas

Request and response bodies of the Triton Cloud API, by name.

## AccountState

The account's standing as its holder sees it. Coarser than the operator's view: every state a payment cannot resolve reads as `on_hold`.

One of:

- `pending`: Waiting on a payment method or a review before it may provision.
- `trial`: Provisioning on trial terms until `trial_ends_at`.
- `trial_expired`: The trial ended. Instances are stopped; a payment method reopens the account.
- `active`: Normal operation.
- `on_hold`: Held by the operator. Only support can lift it.
- `unknown`: A state written by a newer server than this client.

## ActivityActor

Who did a thing, as a tenant may see it.

One of:

- { `kind`: `user`, `user_id`: string (uuid), `username`: string }: A signed-in person. `username` is looked up at read time and is absent when the account no longer exists.
- { `kind`: `api_key`, `user_id`: string (uuid), `username`: string }: An API key. Its owner is named the same way.
- { `kind`: `system` }
- { `kind`: `unknown` }

## ActivityOutcome

How an activity ended.

One of:

- `success` \| `unknown`
- `refused`: Refused by policy or by a client error.
- `failed`: Attempted and failed inside the platform.

## AddressFamily

Address family selector used by [`NewFloatingIp`] to ask the server to allocate from one or the other Phase 0 pool.

Type: `v4` \| `v6`

## AddressPurpose

What an external address range may be handed out for. Declared on the range, never on the pool and never on an individual address.

One of:

- `nat-gateway`: SNAT source address for a VPC NAT gateway.
- `floating-ip`: Tenant-allocatable 1:1 floating IP.
- `external-ip`: Tenant-held external IP.
- `unknown`: An unrecognized wire value decodes to `Unknown`, which is never eligible for any allocation and can never be set. Fail closed.

## AffectedInstancesResponse

Response body for `GET /v1/meta/{scope}/{scope_id}/affected?key=K` — the affected-instances reverse-index. Answers the question "if I edit `key` at this scope, which instances does that change actually flow to, and which are shielded by a narrower override?" See `IMDS_DESIGN.md` §1.5 for the precedence rules.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shadowed` | array of [ShadowedInstance](schemas.md#shadowedinstance) | yes | Instances under the request scope where a narrower scope already overrides this key. Each row names the narrower scope so the UI can render "tenant wins" / "project wins" / "instance wins" at a glance. |
| `value_at_scope` | [MetaValue](schemas.md#metavalue) | no | The value stored at the request scope (`null` when the key is not set there). Returned for context — the UI doesn't have to make a separate `GET /v1/meta/.../entry` call. |
| `wins` | array of [AffectedInstanceRef](schemas.md#affectedinstanceref) | yes | Instances under the request scope where this scope's value is the realized winner (no narrower scope overrides it). |

## ApiKeyScope

One of:

- `booter`
- `full`: Full access — equivalent to authenticating as the owning user. Default when no scope is specified.
- `read_only`: List/get on every resource, plus audit chain reads. Cannot mutate state, mint or delete API keys, or change IdP config. Useful for monitoring agents and read replicas.
- `tenant_write`: Everything [`ApiKeyScope::ReadOnly`] allows, plus the writes a tenant performs on its own resources: projects, VPCs, subnets, instances, disks, floating IPs, images, SSH keys and metadata. This is the tier an ordinary customer's session carries. Before it existed, every non-fleet token minted by identityd floored at `ReadOnly`, so a tenant could sign in and then create nothing. It is a ceiling on the credential, not the tenancy boundary:
- `audit_only`: Audit chain reads only (`audit_list`, `audit_fetch`, `audit_verify`). Useful for compliance pipelines that should see "who did what when" but never the resources themselves.
- `agent`: Provisioning-agent scope: `agent_claim` and `agent_complete` only. A key with this scope cannot read tenant resources or audit events; it can only pull jobs from the queue and
- `ur_enroll`: ur-enrollment endpoint scope: announce ur-discovered nodes, drain the operator-approved setup queue, take the consume-once setup bundle, and report setup complete/failed. Deliberately cannot approve a node for setup or open/close the
- `dnsedge`: triton-dnsedge scope: the DC DNS zone list + record feed reads and nothing else. The Internet-facing daemon's credential yields a read-only, DNS-shaped view even if leaked (external-dns-tls-bootstrap.md §7 data path).
- `certs`: In-zone triton-certs scope: certificate-bundle reads (the §10 renewal poll) plus Health and nothing else. Minted during bootstrap-token redemption so a zone can keep converging on renewals after its one-shot token is burnt. Deliberately excluded from `ReadOnly` semantics: bundle reads carry private key material.

## BuildPlacementMode

Where the Phase-2 NoCloud distro-image build job runs.

The downgrade is lossy — re-serializing `Unknown` emits `"unknown"`, dropping the future mode name — so modes stay additive-only.

One of:

- `any_cn`: Any internet-capable CN may run the build.
- `tagged`: Pin the build to CNs carrying the tag in `tag`.
- `unknown`: A mode written by a newer binary that this one does not know.

## ChallengeMode

Anti-automation gate a [`SignupRequest`] must clear before it is accepted. See `record_solved_challenge` for how a solved challenge is consumed exactly once.

Defaults to [`Self::ProofOfWork`], deliberately not [`Self::None`]: self-signup is closed on every silo today ([`SiloSignupPolicy`]'s `enabled` defaults `false` *and* the cluster-wide `signup_enabled_default` setting defaults `false`), so nothing deployed changes behavior. A policy write that turns signup on without saying anything about a challenge should get the strongest challenge every deployment can run unconditionally, not silently skip it -- the same "guessing wrong opens a hole" reasoning `enabled` documents for its own default.

One of:

- `none`: No challenge. Only sane when signup itself is closed, or an equivalent gate is enforced at another layer (an edge WAF, a closed network).
- `proof-of-work`: A client-side proof-of-work challenge (ALTCHA). No third-party account, no CAPTCHA UX, and no network call the client can be starved of -- the default because it is the one mode every deployment can run without opting into anything external.
- `turnstile`: Cloudflare Turnstile.
- `h-captcha`: hCaptcha.
- `unknown`: Written by a newer binary than this one. Treated the same as an unrecognised [`AdmissionRequirement`]: never satisfiable, so an upgrade a rolling deploy hasn't reached yet cannot be talked into skipping whatever mode a newer binary configured.

## CheckoutLaunch

`POST /v1/onboarding/checkout` response.

**`checkout_url` is a bearer credential.** Whoever holds it can complete the payment page and create a subscription for this account. It goes to the account holder's browser and nowhere else: never into a log, never into an error message, never into an audit payload. That is why `Debug` is written by hand here rather than derived — a derived one would put the URL into every `{:?}` of every struct that ever contains this.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `checkout_url` | string | yes |  |

## CloudinitDatasource

Which cloud-init datasource an image is built to consume, sourced from the IMGAPI manifest tag `org.smartos:cloudinit_datasource`.

One of:

- `nocloud`: NoCloud: the platform builds a 16 MiB cidata seed disk from the `cloud-init:*` customer_metadata keys at zone create.
- `unknown`: Forward compatibility (type-safety rule 5): a tag value this build doesn't recognize. Treated like an absent tag.

## CpuClass

Class of CPU a package sells.

This is the *ask* side — what a customer bought — and is recorded on [`Package`] and [`Instance`] so nothing downstream needs a catalog lookup to know what was purchased.

`Generic` is the only class that can be sold today. The field is present from the first row written because packages are immutable: a package minted without it could never gain one. `#[non_exhaustive]` keeps adding a variant (`HighFrequency`, …) a non-breaking change when such hardware lands.

One of:

- `generic`: No particular CPU requirement; places anywhere.
- `unknown`: Not settable: rejected on package create and update. It exists only so a row written by a newer version stays readable here, and a row carrying it can be read but neither provisioned from nor rewritten.

## CurrentUser

Response body for `GET /v1/me`: who the caller is and what scope their token resolves to.

Deliberately narrower than `UserView`, which is the operator-facing shape. This one is read by the subject of the record, so it carries identity and scope and nothing describing the operator surface: `is_root`, `fleet_admin`, and `capabilities` are all withheld. A customer who can enumerate the capability names learns the shape of a surface they cannot reach, and asks support why they cannot reach it.

`silo_id` and `tenant_id` are the point of the endpoint. Decision 2 makes the token the source of scope, so every `?silo=`/`?tenant=` selector a customer might legitimately pass is undiscoverable until something tells them what their own scope is.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `created_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `federated` | boolean | yes | True when this account authenticates through the silo's identity provider rather than a local password. The issuer and subject behind it stay server-side: they identify the account to the IdP, and the caller already knows which IdP it used. |
| `id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `silo_id` | string (uuid) | no | Silo the tenant belongs to, absent for cluster-wide accounts. |
| `tenant_id` | string (uuid) | no | Owning tenant, absent for cluster-wide accounts. |
| `username` | string | yes |  |

## CustomerMetaScope

The metadata scopes a customer may name on `/v1/meta/...`.

A deliberately narrowed `MetaScope`: the storage enum has four variants and this one has three, the same way a scope selector narrows a storage enum elsewhere on this surface. `Silo` is excluded because a silo spans every tenant in it, so silo-scope metadata is fleet configuration that inherits into tenants that do not own it. That scope lives on the operator mount, `/v1/system/meta/...`, as [`MetaScopePath`]'s four-variant counterpart.

`Tenant` is deliberately *included*. A customer setting tenant-wide metadata that inherits down to their own projects and instances is ordinary use of their own tenancy, not an operator act.

The narrowing is what makes the audience split structural: `silo` on this mount fails to deserialize, so it is refused before any handler runs rather than by a check one handler could forget.

Type: `tenant` \| `project` \| `instance`

## DataDiskTier

The journal tier of a data disk's volume.

One of:

- `performance`: Journals on power-loss-protected NVMe drives.
- `standard`: Journals in files on the node's pool.

## DiskClass

Class of backing storage a package sells.

Deliberately **not** [`StorageTier`], despite the near-identical variant list. The two answer different questions and belong to different directions of travel:

* [`StorageTier`] is agent-published (`tier`) and answers *what is this pool physically made of*. `Mixed` is meaningful there and meaningless in a catalog. * `DiskClass` is customer-facing and answers *what was bought*. `Generic` is meaningful here and meaningless in a capacity report.

Merging them would also put an ask-side value into an enum agents serialize, and would drag `placement::storage_tier_view` — whose `_ =>` arm silently coerces unknown variants to `Mixed` — into the blast radius of every catalog change. The `DiskClass -> StorageTier` mapping belongs in the disk-capacity filter when real class-to-pool resolution lands; that is the correct place for the two vocabularies to meet.

One of:

- `generic`: No particular storage requirement; places anywhere.
- `ssd`: SATA/SAS solid state.
- `nvme`: NVMe solid state.
- `hdd`: Spinning disk.
- `unknown`: Not settable: rejected on package create and update. It exists only so a row written by a newer version stays readable here, and a row carrying it can be read but neither provisioned from nor rewritten.

## DiskKind

What a disk is for. Phase 0 ships only `Boot` disks (auto-created from the instance's image at instance create time). `Data` is reserved for the future multi-disk attach slice.

One of:

- `boot`: Bootable; sourced from an Image. The instance boots from this disk on first start.
- `data`: Blank persistent storage attached to the instance. Reserved for the future multi-disk slice; not yet exercised.

## FirewallRuleUpdate

ICMP type + code pair carried as a struct (instead of `(u8, u8)`) so the JSON schema is OpenAPI v3.0–compatible (tuple arrays are not representable until v3.1). Fields a tenant may change on an existing rule. Every field is optional; an omitted one keeps its value. `source_cidr`, `destination_cidr`, `source_ports`, `destination_ports` and `icmp_type_code` clear when passed as `null` and stay untouched when absent, so the wire distinguishes "leave it" from "remove it".

| `action` | [FirewallAction](schemas.md#firewallaction) | no |  |
| `description` | string | no |  |
| `destination_cidr` | string | no |  |
| `destination_ports` | [FirewallPortRange](schemas.md#firewallportrange) | no |  |
| `destinations` | array of [FirewallTarget](schemas.md#firewalltarget) | no | Replaces the whole list; see `sources`. |
| `direction` | [FirewallDirection](schemas.md#firewalldirection) | no |  |
| `enabled` | boolean | no |  |
| `icmp_type_code` | [FirewallIcmpFilter](schemas.md#firewallicmpfilter) | no |  |
| `name` | string | no |  |
| `priority` | integer (uint16) | no |  |
| `protocol` | [FirewallProtocol](schemas.md#firewallprotocol) | no |  |
| `source_cidr` | string | no | Legacy form of `sources`; ignored when `sources` is also set. |
| `source_ports` | [FirewallPortRange](schemas.md#firewallportrange) | no |  |
| `sources` | array of [FirewallTarget](schemas.md#firewalltarget) | no | Replaces the whole list. Also rewrites `source_cidr`, so a legacy reader sees the single block when there is one. |

## FirewallTarget

One party on a side of a firewall rule.

The words come from the legacy Triton rule language so a tenant who knows `FROM any TO tag role=www` can read the rule unchanged. `AllInstances`, `Instance` and `Tag` name instances. On the side a rule attaches to, `Ip` and `Subnet` name the instances whose address is in the block; that is how a rule is scoped to one subnet. `Any` names no instance, so a rule with only `Any` on its attach side applies to nothing and is refused.

One of:

- { `kind`: `any` }
- { `kind`: `all_instances` }
- { `address`: string, `kind`: `ip` }
- { `cidr`: string, `kind`: `subnet` }
- { `instance_id`: string (uuid), `kind`: `instance` }
- { `key`: string, `kind`: `tag`, `value`: string }

## FloatingIp

Tenant-managed external IP, allocated from a fleet pool and attachable to any NIC in the same project. Persists independent of any single instance: when the attached instance is deleted, the `attached_to` field clears but the FloatingIp itself stays owned by the project and reusable.

Each FloatingIp represents *one* address — the wire shape does not bifurcate IPv4 and IPv6. The address family is implicit in the `address` bits.

Phase 0 invariants vs other clouds:

* **Project-owned, not instance-owned.** Instance delete → auto-detach, never auto-release. (AWS detaches but leaves the IP at the account level, which loses the project-scoping story; we keep the project envelope.) * **Symmetric IPv4 + IPv6.** No "v6 floating IPs are a separate type" wart. * **Atomic attach replaces.** A second attach with a different

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string (ip) | yes | The actual external address. Allocated at create time from the requested family's pool. Immutable for the life of the record. |
| `attached_to` | [FloatingIpAttachment](schemas.md#floatingipattachment) | no | Currently-bound NIC, or `None` if floating. Replaced atomically by `attach`; cleared by `detach` and by the instance-delete cascade. |
| `created_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `description` | string | yes |  |
| `external_nic_tag` | string (uuid) | no | External nic_tag the dataplane egresses/ingresses this FIP on. Derived read-only from `network_id`'s subnet `nic_tag` at create time — never client-set, so a FIP can never carry a nic_tag inconsistent with its subnet (invariant 17). |
| `hosted_cn` | string (uuid) | no | CN currently hosting this FIP's 1:1 NAT termination. Stamped on `attach` from the target instance's `host_cn_uuid`, cleared on `detach` and by the instance-delete cascade. Pins the dataplane claim/release jobs to a concrete CN. |
| `id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `network_id` | string (uuid) | no | External Subnet this address was allocated from, when the FIP was created via the pool/network path (C-3). `None` for legacy `family`-allocated records. Drives `external_nic_tag`. |
| `project_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `tenant_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `updated_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |

Host-compatibility constraints on an [`Image`]. A superset of `Compatibility` — the bundle ingest path copies the manifest's compatibility block in field-for-field (bundle manifests carry no datasource tag, so that field stays `None` there). The per-CN agent enforces these gates at provision time.

NoCloud seed generation is opt-in: the agent emits the datasource only for `Some(Nocloud)`; `None` and `Some(Unknown)` do not enable seed generation. |

## ImageGrant

A single visibility grant on an [`Image`] (Model B). Grants are the legacy IMGAPI `acl`: they widen who can *see* an image without changing its owner (`Image.scope`) or its stable `id`.

There is deliberately no `Global` variant — global visibility is the `Image.public` flag — and no `Project` variant: project-scoped visibility is out of the Model B surface. Wire form matches [`ImageScope`]'s internally-tagged shape (`{"kind":"silo", "silo_id":…}` / `{"kind":"tenant","tenant_id":…}`) so a grant and an owner scope read the same on the wire.

One of:

- { `kind`: `silo`, `silo_id`: string (uuid) }
- { `kind`: `tenant`, `tenant_id`: string (uuid) }

| `operation_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

## ImageInstanceRef

One row of the "instances using this image" blast radius (`GET /v1/images/{image}/instances`). Trimmed to the fields an operator needs to reason about the consequence of editing / moving / deleting an image: which instance, its display name, and its current lifecycle state.

`state` is the flat snake_case discriminant of the instance's `LifecycleState` (`pending`, `running`, …), and `reason` carries the failure detail when (and only when) `state == "failed"`. The state is deliberately flattened to a top-level string rather than embedding the internally-tagged `LifecycleState` directly: a `state: LifecycleState` field would serialize as a *nested* `{"state":{"state":"running"}}` object, which every consumer of this trimmed projection would then have to un-nest. Keeping it flat matches the on-the-wire contract the blast-radius UI reads (`{id,name,state,reason?}`).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `reason` | string | no | Failure detail; present only when `state == "failed"`. |
| `state` | string | yes | Flat lifecycle discriminant (snake_case): `pending`, `provisioning`, `running`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `failed`. |

## ImageOwnerTarget

Owner + initial visibility for a Model-B image create (`POST /v1/system/image-imports`).

The variant names the owner scope; the server sets the image's owner (`scope`) and initial visibility from it: * `global` — owner `Public`, `public == true`. ROOT ONLY. * `system` — owner `System`: platform infrastructure images, visible to operators only and never listed or bootable for a tenant. ROOT ONLY. * `silo` — owner `Silo { silo_id }`, visible to the silo. * `tenant` — owner `Tenant { tenant_id }`, visible to the tenant.

There is deliberately no `project` / `user` variant: those scopes are out of the Model-B image surface.

One of:

- { `kind`: `global` }
- { `kind`: `system` }
- { `kind`: `silo`, `silo_id`: string (uuid) }
- { `kind`: `tenant`, `tenant_id`: string (uuid) }

## ImagePolicy

Request body for `PUT /v1/images/{image}/policy` (convention 7).

The whole visibility policy, not a delta: `grants` replaces the image's grant set outright, and `[]` revokes everything. Duplicates are collapsed rather than rejected, because a set with a repeat in it names the same policy as one without.

There is no `public` field. Global visibility is the owner (`scope == Public`), changed by `image_promote`; carrying it here too would let one request describe two different visibilities.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `grants` | array of [ImageGrant](schemas.md#imagegrant) | yes | Silos and tenants that may see this image beyond its owner. |

## ImageScope

Visibility scope of an [`Image`]. The variant determines who can see and use the image: `Public` is everyone (including anonymous probes on the public listing endpoint); `Silo` is every member of any tenant under that silo; `Tenant` is every member of that tenant; `Project` is every tenant member with project access (Phase 0: every tenant member); `User` is one specific user.

The variant carries everything the visibility predicate needs — there are no denormalised silo_id / tenant_id fields on `Image`. For `Project`, the resolver looks up the project to derive its tenant + silo when needed; for `Tenant`, the resolver looks up the tenant for its silo when needed. Cold path; correctness > one extra read.

One of:

- { `kind`: `public` }
- { `kind`: `system` }
- { `kind`: `silo`, `silo_id`: string (uuid) }
- { `kind`: `tenant`, `tenant_id`: string (uuid) }
- { `kind`: `project`, `project_id`: string (uuid) }
- { `kind`: `user`, `user_id`: string (uuid) }

## ImageScopeSelector

Owner scope selector for `GET /v1/images?scope=...`.

One variant per collection the six pre-Wave-2 image paths served, and no more. Unlike [`SshKeyScopeSelector`] this does carry a `user` variant, because `/v1/auth/images` folds into `/v1/images` rather than surviving as a separate collection the way `/v1/auth/ssh-keys` does.

One of:

- `public`: Images owned by no scope, readable by everyone.
- `silo`: Images owned by `?silo=`, and only those. Not a union, and in particular not the silo's view of what it can use: it carries neither `Public` images nor images merely granted to the silo. A tenant's own listing already covers grants to its silo, and `/v1/system/images` is the operator read that sees every grant.
- `tenant`: Images a member of `?tenant=` can use: `Public`, the tenant's silo's, the tenant's own, and anything granted to either.
- `project`: Images a member of `?project=` can use: the `tenant` union plus the project's own.
- `user`: The caller's own `User`-owned images. Takes no selector: the owner is read from the credential, never from the query.

## Instance

Tenant compute instance. Project-scoped; references one image (boot media), one subnet (network attach point), and zero-or-more SSH keys (injected into authorized_keys at provisioning time).

Phase 0 ships only the metadata + lifecycle state machine. The actual provisioning is faked synchronously inside the create handler; a future slice introduces the intent queue and stub executor that will become the swap-out point for a real `tritonagent`.

Several fields that real cloud instances carry are deliberately omitted in v0: cloud-init userdata, tags/labels, affinity rules, console URL, migration history. Each will land as the consuming use case ships. The hosting CN is recorded once placement lands so subsequent lifecycle jobs return to the same SmartOS host.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `billing_id` | string (uuid) | no | [`Package`] version this instance was provisioned from; `None` for a free-form shape and for every record written before packages existed. Never re-pointed by a resize. The uuid identifies a specific immutable package *version*, which is what an invoice references; moving it would retroactively change what a customer was billed for. |
| `brand` | [InstanceBrand](schemas.md#instancebrand) | no | SmartOS brand this instance's host-side VM runs as. Derived from the boot image's compatibility block at create time; `NotApplicable` for older records and explicit-fields images. |
| `cpu` | integer (uint32) | yes | Number of vCPUs. |
| `cpu_class` | [CpuClass](schemas.md#cpuclass) | no | Class of CPU this instance was sold. Denormalised from the package (or defaulted for a free-form shape) so placement and future metering never need a catalog lookup. |
| `created_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `description` | string | yes |  |
| `disk_class` | [DiskClass](schemas.md#diskclass) | no | Class of storage backing this instance's boot disk. Lives on the instance rather than on [`Disk`] because the boot disk is 1:1 with the instance and the placement request is built from this row; a per-disk class lands with data disks. |
| `host_cn_uuid` | string (uuid) | no | SmartOS compute node that owns this instance's host-side VM. `None` is retained for in-process test/stub jobs and legacy records created before tenant placement existed. Real M1 deployments assign this before the first Provision job is enqueued. |
| `id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `image_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Boot image. An instance can only name an image its owner can see; a reference to one it cannot see answers `NotFound`. |
| `memory_bytes` | integer (uint64) | yes | Memory budget in bytes. |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `primary_subnet_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Subnet the instance's primary NIC attaches to. Phase 0 auto-creates a NIC at provisioning time; a future slice adds explicit NIC records that operators can manage separately. Subnet must live in a VPC inside this project. |
| `project_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `provenance` | [InstanceProvenance](schemas.md#instanceprovenance) | no | Who owns this instance. See [`InstanceProvenance`]. Not settable through [`NewInstance`]: it is threaded separately via `PlatformInstanceSpec`, because `NewInstance` is the literal request body and a caller-settable provenance would let a tenant mint an instance that is hidden from their own list, uncharged against quota, and refused to every lifecycle verb. |
| `ssh_key_ids` | array of string (uuid) | yes | SSH keys to inject into the instance's authorized_keys at first boot. Each key id must live in the same silo as the instance. May be empty (no key injection). |
| `state` | [LifecycleState](schemas.md#lifecyclestate) | yes |  |
| `tags` | map of string | no | Free-form labels. Firewall rules select instances by tag, so a tag change must reach the dataplane; the handler that writes tags bumps the VPC port generations. |
| `tenant_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `time_state_updated` | string (date-time) | no | When `state` last changed value. Not derivable from `updated_at`, which every mutation bumps: placement (`set_instance_host_cn`) and brand derivation both touch it without changing the state. A client polling after a `202` needs the difference to tell "the transition has not started yet" from "it ran and the instance is back in the state it left". `None` on a row written before this field existed. Left deliberately absent rather than backfilled from `created_at`, which would assert a state age the row cannot support; the first transition after the upgrade stamps it. |
| `updated_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |

## InstanceBrand

SmartOS brand the instance's host-side VM runs as.

One of:

- `bhyve`
- `kvm`: `kvm` HVM zone (legacy hypervisor; serial + VNC consoles).
- `lx`: `lx` Linux-syscall zone (serial via the zone console only).
- `joyent-minimal`: `joyent-minimal` native SmartOS zone (serial via the zone console only).
- `fhyve`: `fhyve` microVM: a sandbox guest with its own kernel. Needs hardware virtualization but has no framebuffer, so it is serial only.
- `not-applicable`: Brand not recorded / not recognised. The console surface treats this as "serial only".

## InstanceProvenance

Who owns an [`Instance`].

One of:

- `tenant`: Created by a customer through the tenant API. The default, so a row written before this field existed reads as tenant-owned.
- `platform-ssh-relay`: The per-subnet SSH-broker relay.
- `platform-nat-gateway`: A VPC NAT gateway relay zone. A platform instance like the SSH relay: hidden from tenants, single-NIC, and its port carries the NAT relay dataplane posture. The owning gateway is found through its `NatGatewayZoneRef.instance_id`.
- `platform-load-balancer`: A load balancer zone. Hidden from tenants like the gateways; its load balancer is found through `LbIncarnation::instance_id`.
- `platform-nas-gateway`: An NFS gateway zone serving a VPC's tenant filesystems. Hidden from tenants like the other gateways; its set is found through `NasGateway::instance_id`.
- `tenant-sandbox`: The instance that backs a sandbox, and the rules written for it. A sandbox is not an ordinary instance: it is driven through the sandbox API, it is hidden from the instance list, and the rules that bound what it may reach are written by the platform rather than by the tenant. Unlike the access grant above, these rules are not consent: they are the boundary the sandbox runs inside, so a tenant can neither edit nor delete them.
- `unknown`: Never a legal write value; it exists only so a row written by a newer version stays readable. `is_tenant_owned` is a positive allow-list precisely so this variant stays hidden from tenants rather than becoming visible and deletable.

## InstanceSizingMode

Which instance sizing forms a silo's tenants may use when creating instances. Enforced synchronously at the instance-create API edge.

One of:

- `package-only`: Only package-based creates are allowed; a free-form request (no `package_id`) is denied.
- `free-form-only`: Only free-form creates are allowed; a `package_id` is denied.
- `package-or-free-form`: Either sizing form is allowed. The product default, preserving pre-feature behavior. The caller may choose either form; both are not required.
- `unknown`: A mode written by a newer binary that this one does not know.

## LifecycleState

Lifecycle state of a tenant instance. The state machine:

```text create ↓ Pending ──→ Provisioning ──┬→ Running ←──┬── Stopped │             │      ↑ │             │      │ ↓             ↓      │ Failed        Stopping─┘ ```

A create answers with the instance in `pending`; a start, stop, restart or delete answers with it in the transitional state. Read the instance until it settles.

Requested transitions: start (Stopped → Pending), stop (Running → Stopping), restart (Running → Stopping → Pending), delete (Stopped or Failed → Deleting, then gone). Transitions the platform reports: Pending → Provisioning → Running, Provisioning → Failed, Stopping → Stopped.

Delete is allowed only from Stopped or Failed; deleting a Running instance returns 409.

One of:

- { `state`: `pending` }: Newly created; not yet picked up by an agent.
- { `state`: `provisioning` }: An agent has claimed the provisioning job and is working.
- { `state`: `running` }: Up and running.
- { `state`: `stopping` }: Stop requested; agent is winding down.
- { `state`: `stopped` }: Fully stopped; safe to delete or restart.
- { `state`: `deleting` }: Delete accepted; the instance goes away when the platform has released it.
- { `reason`: string, `state`: `failed` }: Unrecoverable error. Inspect `reason`; the instance must be deleted.

## LifecycleStateKind

Discriminant-only companion to [`LifecycleState`]. Used by `Store::transition_instance_lifecycle`'s `expected_from` parameter so callers can name "any Failed state" without committing to a specific `reason` string, and as the typed `?state=` filter on the instance list surfaces.

The wire names match [`LifecycleState`]'s variant names, so `?state=running` selects the same rows the `state` field reports.

Type: `pending` \| `provisioning` \| `running` \| `stopping` \| `stopped` \| `deleting` \| `failed`

## LoadBalancerState

One of:

- `deleting` \| `unknown`
- `provisioning`: Created; a saga is placing the zone.
- `ready`: Every listener serves the current revision and is reachable.
- `serving`: Serving, but reachability from outside has not been confirmed.
- `degraded`: Serving, with at least one route that has no healthy member.
- `unavailable`: Nothing is serving.
- `failed`: The last operation failed; `condition` says why.

## MetaValue

`value` is an arbitrary JSON value (strings are the common case; IMDS serves a JSON string as `text/plain` and any other JSON as `application/json`). The two boolean flags control the in-VM view: `guest_visible` gates whether IMDS exposes the key at all, and `guest_writable` gates whether the in-VM `PUT` may modify it (only ever true for `guest/*` keys at instance scope on a writeback- enabled instance — enforced by [`validate_meta_entry`] and the store layer).

| `guest_writable` | boolean | yes | The in-VM IMDS `PUT` may write this key. Only ever true for `guest/*` keys at instance scope on a writeback-enabled instance. |
| `updated_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `updated_by` | string | yes | Who last wrote it: a user UUID, `"guest:<instance-id>"` for an in-VM `PUT`, or `"system"` for seed values. |

## NatGateway

Project-owned VPC egress point. A NAT gateway reserves one public address from the same Phase 0 public pool used by [`FloatingIp`], then downstream edge realization decides where and how that address is programmed.

The stored record carries `desired_generation`; `realized` is computed from the realization rows at read time.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `condition` | string | no | Short operator-facing reason for Degraded / Failed. Operator vocabulary; never rendered to a tenant. |
| `created_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `description` | string | yes |  |
| `desired_generation` | integer (uint64) | yes | Monotonic desired-state generation, bumped in the same transaction as every wire-affecting change. |
| `external_mac` | string | no | MAC of the gateway's external interface, minted in the same transaction that allocates the address. Pinned onto the external vnic so a re-place onto another CN keeps the upstream router's ARP entry valid. |
| `external_network_id` | string (uuid) | no | External range the address came from. Drives the zone's external NIC: nic_tag, VLAN, prefix, upstream gateway, MTU, resolvers. |
| `external_nic_tag` | string (uuid) | no | Derived read-only from the range at create, never client-set, so a gateway can never carry a nic_tag inconsistent with its range. |
| `family` | [AddressFamily](schemas.md#addressfamily) | yes | Public address family requested at create time. |
| `id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `inside_ipv4` | string (ipv4) | no | The gateway's address inside `subnet_id`: an ordinary allocated address, never the synthetic virtual-gateway slot. |
| `inside_ipv6` | string (ipv6) | no |  |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `placement_epoch` | integer (uint64) | no | Monotonic fencing token, incremented on every (re)placement. |
| `project_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `public_address` | string (ip) | yes | Public source address reserved for egress. Allocated at create, released at delete, stable across re-placement and across periods of inactivity. |
| `realized` | [RealizedNetworkState](schemas.md#realizednetworkstate) | yes | Read-time projection of the per-realizer rows for this NAT gateway. This is not stored as a denormalized field. |
| `state` | [NatGatewayState](schemas.md#natgatewaystate) | no |  |
| `subnet_id` | string (uuid) | no | VPC subnet the gateway's inside port lands in. `None` only while `Pending`, before any subnet exists. |
| `tenant_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `undesired_since` | string (date-time) | no | When the desired-zone predicate last went false; drives the reap hysteresis. Cleared when the predicate goes true again. |
| `updated_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `vpc_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `zone` | [NatGatewayZoneRef](schemas.md#natgatewayzoneref) | no | The zone realizing this gateway, when one is placed. |

## NatGatewayState

One of:

- `materializing` \| `reaping` \| `unknown`
- `pending`: Record exists, public address reserved, no zone wanted yet: nothing routes to this gateway, or the VPC has no subnet.
- `active`: A realizer reported Applied at `desired_generation` and `placement_epoch`.
- `degraded`: Zone exists but egress may be down. `condition` says why.
- `failed`: Repair budget exhausted, or an operator-only condition blocks progress. The reconciler will not act again until cleared.

Request body for allocating a new FloatingIp. The address source is one of three mutually exclusive selectors:

* `network_id` — allocate the lowest-free address from a specific External subnet (C-3, preferred); * `pool_id` — walk a [`NetworkPool`]'s ordered networks and take the first free address (C-3); * `family` — the legacy Phase-0 path that draws from the hardcoded `FLOATING_IP_V*_POOL`.

At most one may be set; the server rejects a request with more

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | string | no |  |
| `family` | [AddressFamily](schemas.md#addressfamily) | no | Legacy Phase-0 family selector. Mutually exclusive with `network_id` / `pool_id`. `None` only when one of those is set. |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `network_id` | string (uuid) | no | External subnet to allocate from. Stamps `FloatingIp::network_id` and derives `external_nic_tag`. Mutually exclusive with the other two selectors. |
| `pool_id` | string (uuid) | no | Network pool to allocate from (walks its ordered networks). Mutually exclusive with the other two selectors. |

## NewScopedImage

Request body for `POST /v1/images`.

The owner arrives in the body rather than in the path, which is what collapsed the five scoped create paths into this one. It is spelled as `ImageScope`, the same tagged union the created image echoes back in its `scope` field, so a caller reads and writes one shape rather than two.

`kind: "user"` is accepted, unlike [`NewScopedSshKey`], because `/v1/auth/images` folded in here rather than surviving. The `user_id` it carries must be the caller's own: the server compares it against the credential and refuses anything else, so naming somebody else as the owner is a `400`, never a create.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `compatibility` | [ImageCompatibility](schemas.md#imagecompatibility) | no | Optional host-compatibility constraints. Populated by the server when an image is registered via the bundle ingest path; absent when the operator passed individual fields by hand. The per-CN agent enforces these when `Some`. |
| `description` | string | no |  |
| `id` | string (uuid) | no | Optional UUID to pin for the new image. When `None` (the usual case), the server derives the UUID deterministically from `(scope, sha256)` via [`derive_image_id`] — same content in the same scope always yields the same id across hosts and replays, so the per-CN agent's content-addressed ZFS dataset (`zones/<image_id>`) collapses identical bytes into one import. Different scopes registering the same content yield distinct ids (no cross-scope collisions). |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `os` | string | yes |  |
| `scope` | [ImageScope](schemas.md#imagescope) | yes |  |
| `sha256` | string | yes |  |
| `size_bytes` | integer (uint64) | yes |  |
| `source_url` | string | no |  |
| `version` | string | yes |  |

## NewScopedSshKey

Request body for `POST /v1/ssh-keys`.

The owner arrives in the body rather than in the path, which is what collapsed the four scoped create paths into this one. It is spelled as `SshKeyScope`, the same tagged union the created key echoes back in its `scope` field, so a caller reads and writes one shape rather than two.

`kind: "user"` is refused with `400`: a user-owned key is created at `/v1/auth/ssh-keys`, which resolves the owner from the credential instead of taking a `user_id` a caller could point at somebody else.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | string | no |  |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `public_key` | string | yes |  |
| `scope` | [SshKeyScope](schemas.md#sshkeyscope) | yes |  |

## Nic

Per-instance network interface. Auto-created at instance create time with a single "primary" NIC; multi-NIC attach/detach is a future slice. Mirrors what the dataplane (OPTE per-NIC config) will eventually consume — guest MAC, primary IPv4/IPv6 in the subnet's CIDR.

Phase 0 stores only the per-NIC fields the agent needs to open the overlay attachment for an instance:

* `mac` — guest MAC address. Locally-administered (`02:` prefix) + 5 random bytes; uniqueness is rack-wide. * `primary_ipv4` / `primary_ipv6` — addresses allocated from the parent subnet's CIDR. Each family is `Some` only if the subnet has a CIDR for that family.

External IPs, attached_subnets (other-subnet routing), and firewall rules are *not* on the NIC record — they live on future External-IP / Route / FirewallRule resources.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `created_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `instance_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `mac` | string | yes | Guest MAC, formatted as 6 lowercase hex bytes separated by colons (e.g. `02:1a:b3:cd:ef:42`). |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `primary_ipv4` | string (ipv4) | no | Primary IPv4 from `subnet.ipv4_block`. `None` if the parent subnet is IPv6-only. |
| `primary_ipv6` | string (ipv6) | no | Primary IPv6 from `subnet.ipv6_block`. `None` if the parent subnet is IPv4-only. |
| `project_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `subnet_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `tenant_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `vpc_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

## OnboardingStatus

`GET /v1/onboarding` response: what the signed-in account must still do before it can provision, and whether this deployment can take it there right now.

Tenancy is the caller's own, taken from the verified principal. There is no selector on the route and none in this type, which is what keeps a browser from aiming a billing read at another tenant.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account_state` | [AccountState](schemas.md#accountstate) | yes | Where the account stands. |
| `can_provision` | boolean | yes | The account may create resources today. |
| `checkout_available` | boolean | yes | `POST /v1/onboarding/checkout` can produce a payment page for this account right now. `false` when the deployment has no billing provider configured, when the account did not arrive through signup and so has no billing contact on file, or when a payment would not convert the account. |
| `payment_method_on_file` | boolean | yes | A payment method was verified, or an invoice paid, for this account. |
| `payment_required` | boolean | yes | The account's admission requires a payment method it has not supplied yet. |
| `resources_deleted_at` | string (date-time) | no | After this, the account's stopped instances may be deleted. Set only while `account_state` is `trial_expired`. |
| `trial_ends_at` | string (date-time) | no | When the trial ends. Set only while `account_state` is `trial`. |

## Package

A provisionable instance specification: the vNext answer to legacy Triton's package/SKU.

**Immutable once written, and never deleted.** `active` is the one mutable field. Editing a package means minting a new row with a new `id` and `version + 1` (see the store's `update_package`), because a package is a billing source of truth: rate cards reference package ids, and an instance provisioned six months ago must still resolve to the exact shape and price it was sold at. Legacy PAPI offered a `force=true` bypass of both immutability and deletion; there is deliberately no equivalent here, and `(silo_id, name, version)` uniqueness is a store constraint rather than a convention.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `active` | boolean | yes | Offerable for new provisions. The one mutable field. At most one active version per `(silo_id, name)` — the name index is authoritative for lookup, and this flag exists so reading a package by id can report a retired version without a reverse lookup. Both are written in the same transaction. An inactive package stays readable and rateable forever, but cannot be provisioned from. |
| `cpu` | integer (uint32) | yes | Number of vCPUs. Same units as `cpu`, so resolving a package into a create request is a field copy. |
| `cpu_class` | [CpuClass](schemas.md#cpuclass) | no |  |
| `created_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `default_disks` | array of [NewDisk](schemas.md#newdisk) | no | The disks an instance of the package gets unless its create names its own: an explicit boot entry replaces this one's. |
| `description` | string | yes |  |
| `disk_bytes` | integer (uint64) | yes | Boot-disk size in bytes. Same units as `disk_bytes`. Packages size the boot disk only — data disks remain separate [`Disk`] resources with their own lifecycle. |
| `disk_class` | [DiskClass](schemas.md#diskclass) | no |  |
| `group` | string | no | Free-form label for catalog grouping ("general-purpose", "hicpu"). Purely presentational. |
| `id` | string (uuid) | yes | Unique per *version*. Lands in `Instance::billing_id`, in the zone's `billing-id` attr, and in future metering events. |
| `kind` | [PackageKind](schemas.md#packagekind) | no | What the package sizes: a VM or a sandbox. A create of one kind cannot use a package of the other. |
| `memory_bytes` | integer (uint64) | yes | Memory budget in bytes. Same units as `memory_bytes`. |
| `name` | string | yes | Family name, stable across versions. `(silo_id, name)` is what an operator provisions by; `(silo_id, name, version)` is unique. |
| `silo_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Owning silo — the brand, catalog, and billing boundary. A rate card prices the catalog of exactly one silo, so a package with no silo would be unpriceable. Packages may be cloned across silos; ids stay silo-local so pricing and lifecycle never entangle brands. |
| `traits` | map of [TraitValue](schemas.md#traitvalue) | no | The CN traits an instance of the package places by, as legacy PAPI package traits did: a CN takes it only when the CN's trait keys are exactly these (plus the class keys) and every value matches. Copied onto the instance at create. `cpu-class` and `disk-class` come from the class fields and cannot be set here. |
| `version` | integer (uint32) | yes | Bumped on each supersession. Load-bearing: half the uniqueness constraint above. |
| `visible_to` | array of string (uuid) | no | Tenants this package is visible to. Empty (the default) means every tenant in the silo. Non-empty means *hidden* from all others, not merely unprovisionable — private and negotiated shapes must not leak through a catalog listing. |

## PackageKind

What a [`Package`] sizes.

One of:

- `vm`: An instance created through the instance API.
- `sandbox`: A sandbox. Sandboxes are sized only by packages of this kind.
- `unknown`: A kind this server does not know.

## Project

Sub-tenancy boundary inside a tenant. Workload resources (instances, volumes, networks) nest under projects.

E-3 re-parented projects from `silo_id` to `tenant_id`: the silo brand-level container owns one or more tenants; tenants own projects; projects own workloads. The owning silo, if needed, is derivable via `silo_id`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `created_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `description` | string | yes |  |
| `id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `tenant_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

## Quota

Per-project resource quota. Singleton: each project has at most one quota record. Set with PUT, read with GET, remove with DELETE. An absent record does not mean "unlimited": it means "no project-level override", and the effective limit then comes from the owning silo's [`SiloQuotaDefaults`], which is itself absent (and therefore unlimited) for every silo that predates signup.

Enforced at instance-create inside the same FDB transaction that writes the instance, against the maintained [`ProjectUsage`] counter, so two concurrent creates cannot both pass.

Limits count what the project *holds*, not what it is *using*: an instance counts against `instance_limit`, `cpu_limit`, `memory_bytes`, and `disk_bytes` from create until delete, in every lifecycle state. A stopped instance keeps its dataset on the CN's zpool, its name, its NICs and IPs, and its boot disk, none of which the fleet can resell, so quota measures allocation. It also means starting a stopped instance can never fail on quota.

Quota is admission control on an increase, not an invariant on stored state. Lowering a limit below current usage leaves the project over its cap and refuses the next create; nothing is reaped. Reclaiming a paying tenant's running workloads because an operator mistyped a limit would be worse than the gap.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cpu_limit` | integer (uint32) | yes | Maximum total vCPUs across all instances in the project. |
| `disk_bytes` | integer (uint64) | yes | Maximum total disk across all instances + volumes in the project, in bytes. |
| `filesystem_bytes` | integer (uint64) | no | Maximum provisioned filesystem bytes in the project. |
| `filesystem_limit` | integer (uint32) | no | Maximum filesystems in the project, every state counted. |
| `instance_limit` | integer (uint32) | yes | Maximum number of instances the project may hold, counting every lifecycle state. |
| `load_balancer_limit` | integer (uint32) | no | Maximum load balancers in the project, every state counted. Each runs a zone and a public one holds a public address. |
| `memory_bytes` | integer (uint64) | yes | Maximum total memory across all instances in the project, in bytes. |
| `nat_gateway_limit` | integer (uint32) | no | Maximum NAT gateways in the project, every lifecycle state counted. Not optional: the VPC toggle will be default-on, so each gateway reserves a scarce public address, and the bound must exist before the faucet does. |
| `project_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `tenant_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `updated_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |

## Realization

Per-realizer realization row. One per `(resource, realizer)` tuple; written by `Store::record_network_realization` and read back by `Store::list_network_realizations`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `generation` | integer (uint64) | yes | Generation the realizer reports for the resource. Monotonic per `(resource, realizer)`: a write with `generation < existing.generation` is rejected with `StoreError::Conflict` (the "backward report" case the Agent C contract calls out). |
| `last_reported_at` | string (date-time) | yes | Wall-clock time the row was last upserted by the realizer. |
| `message` | string | no |  |
| `realizer` | [RealizerId](schemas.md#realizerid) | yes | Which CN or edge cluster reported this row. |
| `status` | [RealizationStatus](schemas.md#realizationstatus) | yes | Realizer-side outcome at this generation. |

## RealizationStatus

Outcome a realizer reports at a given generation. The variant set is deliberately small in v1: `Accepted` for "agent received the blueprint and handed it to its dataplane" (Agent B's `accepted_generation`); `Applied` for "dataplane confirmed the generation active" (the canonical terminal report); `Failed` for terminal apply failure with a short message. The enum is `#[non_exhaustive]` so post-v1 additions (e.g. `Compiling`, `Pending`) can land without breaking downstream matches.

One of:

- `applied`
- `accepted`: The realizer accepted the work and handed the blueprint to its backing dataplane. Aligns with Agent B's
- `failed`: The realizer failed to converge to this generation. The associated message should describe the phase (image fetch, blueprint apply, port start, ...).

## RealizedMetaEntry

One leaf of the realized view: the effective key + value + the scope provenance (`silo|tenant|project|instance|system`). The computed system keys (`meta-data/*`, `triton/system/*`) appear with `from = system`; everything else with the storage scope that won the precedence merge. See `IMDS_DESIGN.md` §1.5.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | [MetaProvenance](schemas.md#metaprovenance) | yes |  |
| `key` | string | yes |  |
| `value` | [MetaValue](schemas.md#metavalue) | yes |  |

## RealizedNetworkState

Rolled-up realization view of a single network resource. Computed at read time from the resource's `desired_generation` field plus the per-realizer rows in the `network_realization/...` keyspace.

**Not a denormalization.** The resource record stores `desired_generation: u64` directly; this view is synthesized by `from_rows` when the resource is serialized for a wire response. Storing the rolled-up view would drift from the per-realizer rows on every realizer report.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `applied_generation` | integer (uint64) | no | Highest generation any realizer has reported with [`RealizationStatus::Applied`]. `None` if no realizer has applied anything yet. Useful as a coarse "did anything take?" signal; "did the dataplane converge everywhere?" requires inspecting `realizations` against the expected realizer set. |
| `desired_generation` | integer (uint64) | yes |  |
| `realizations` | array of [Realization](schemas.md#realization) | yes | Per-realizer rows, sorted by `(realizer.kind_tag(), realizer.id())` for deterministic output. |

## RealizerId

Identity of a realizer reporting a [`Realization`]. v1 ships `Cn` (per-server `tritonagent`, identified by SmartOS `server_uuid`) and `EdgeCluster` (firehyve/fhrun-managed edge microVMs, populated when Agent E begins reporting).

Wire shape: `{ "kind": "cn", "id": "<uuid>" }` / `{ "kind": "edge_cluster", "id": "<uuid>" }`.

One of:

- { `id`: string (uuid), `kind`: `cn` }: SmartOS compute node identified by its `server_uuid`.
- { `id`: string (uuid), `kind`: `edge_cluster` }: Firehyve / fhrun-managed edge cluster identified by its `EdgeCluster.id`. Reserved for Agent E reporting; the reference type lands in H-12.

## ResultsPage_for_DiskView

`items` is the rows for this page; `next_page` is an opaque cursor the caller passes back as `?page_token=...` to fetch the next page, or `None` when the result set is exhausted.

**A short page does not mean the end.** Only `next_page == null` does. Endpoints whose selectors are not all expressible as an index range filter the rows they read, so a page can come back under `limit` while more matches remain further along. Endpoints whose selectors are not all expressible as an index range filter the rows they read, so a page can come back under `limit` while more matches remain further along. Stopping on a short page would silently truncate those listings.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | array of [SandboxSnapshot](schemas.md#sandboxsnapshot) | yes |  |
| `next_page` | string | no |  |

## RouteTarget

Route target. Post-v1 variants such as peering, interconnect, and site-to-site VPN can be added without changing the existing wire shape.

One of:

- { `kind`: `blackhole` }: Drop without an ICMP response.
- { `kind`: `reject` }: Drop with ICMP unreachable.
- { `kind`: `virtual_gateway` }: Send to the VPC virtual gateway.
- { `kind`: `nat_gateway`, `nat_gateway_id`: string (uuid) }: Send to a NAT gateway in the same VPC.
- { `floating_ip_id`: string (uuid), `kind`: `floating_ip` }: Reserved for system-installed routes. Public v1 API rejects this target at the edge.

## SandboxDesktopInput

Request body for `POST /v1/sandboxes/{sandbox}/desktop/input`: one action, as a computer-use agent sends it.

One of:

- { `action`: `move`, `x`: integer (uint32), `y`: integer (uint32) }: Move the pointer to `x`, `y` in display pixels.
- { `action`: `click`, `button`: [SandboxDesktopButton](schemas.md#sandboxdesktopbutton), `count`: integer (uint8), `x`: integer (uint32), `y`: integer (uint32) }: Click at `x`, `y`. `count` is 1 to 3.
- { `action`: `scroll`, `steps`: integer (int8) }: Turn the wheel. `steps` is notches, -10 to 10 and not 0; positive scrolls up.
- { `action`: `key`, `keys`: string }: Press a key chord, such as `ctrl+c`, `Return` or `alt+Tab`.
- { `action`: `type`, `text`: string }: Type text. US keyboard layout, printable ASCII, newline and tab.

What a fork clones from.

## SandboxLifecycle

| `ttl_s` | integer (uint64) | no | Seconds from creation to the deadline; `null` means none. |

## SandboxLifecycleSpec

The lifecycle a caller sets. Every field is optional so a create can take the template defaults.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auto_resume` | boolean | no | Start or resume a stopped or paused sandbox when a request reaches it: an exec, a file call, a code run, or traffic on a preview URL. Without it, those answer `409 SandboxNotRunning`. |
| `idle_timeout_s` | integer (uint64) | no | Seconds without activity before `on_deadline` is applied. Guest CPU and IO count as activity, so a long build is never idle. Omitted or `0` disables the idle timeout. |
| `on_deadline` | [SandboxDeadlineAction](schemas.md#sandboxdeadlineaction) | no | What happens at the deadline or the idle timeout. |
| `ttl_s` | integer (uint64) | no | Seconds from creation to the deadline. Omitted or `0` means the deployment default. |

## SandboxNetwork

Outbound and inbound network policy. Egress and ingress are denied unless a list allows them, and allow beats deny where both match. A refused connection fails at the first packet, so the guest sees the refusal at once.

The document is replaced whole on write: an omitted list is cleared, never kept.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_in` | array of string | no | CIDRs that may reach the guest. |
| `allow_out` | array of string | no | CIDRs, IPv4 or IPv6, the guest may reach. |
| `allow_out_domains` | array of string | no | DNS names the guest may reach. A leading `*.` matches every name below it (`*.github.com` matches `api.github.com`, not `github.com`). The guest resolves names through the sandbox's own resolver only, so a name not allowed here does not resolve. |
| `deny_out` | array of string | no | CIDRs the guest may not reach. |
| `deny_out_domains` | array of string | no | DNS names the guest may not reach, in the same form. |

## SandboxState

Where a sandbox is in its life. A client that polls this value must accept a state it does not know: states are added without a new version of the document.

One of:

- `pending`: Accepted; nothing runs yet.
- `placing`: A node is being chosen.
- `starting`: The guest is booting.
- `running`: The guest answers.
- `stopping`: The guest is being stopped; the filesystem is kept.
- `stopped`: Stopped; `start` boots it again with the filesystem it had.
- `pausing`: Guest memory is being saved.
- `paused`: Memory and filesystem are kept; `resume` continues the guest where it was.
- `resuming`: Saved memory is being restored.
- `forking`: Children are being cloned from it.
- `snapshotting`: A snapshot is being taken.
- `resizing`: Its resources are being changed.
- `deleting`: It is being removed.
- `deleted`: Removed. Reads answer `404` soon after.
- `failed`: A transition failed; `error` says why.
- `unknown`: A state this client does not know.

| `force` | boolean | no | `false` asks the guest to shut down and waits; `true` halts it. |

## SignupCompleteResult

`POST /v1/silos/{silo_id}/signup/{request_id}/complete` success body.

Account continuation only: what the caller needs to finish getting into the account it now has, and nothing else.

There is deliberately no billing field. Signup no longer creates a billing customer or opens a checkout session, so there is no payment URL to hand back and no way for an unreachable payment provider to stop an account from being created. Paying is a separate, authenticated flow the account holder reaches after signing in; the tenant is `Pending` and cannot provision until it clears its silo's admission policy.

By the time this type is on the wire, `tenant_id` names a REAL tenant. The one failure that can happen after it exists -- the sign-in ticket could not be minted -- is deliberately NOT representable here: it answers with a distinct `ErrorCode` instead of a 200 with a null field, precisely so a caller cannot mistake it for an ordinary success. The same call may then simply be retried; it returns this same `tenant_id` with a fresh ticket.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `registration_ticket` | string | yes | The single-use `identityd` registration ticket. Always present when this type is on the wire at all -- see the type doc for why the ticket-unavailable case is a distinct error response, never a `None` here. |
| `tenant_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

## SignupConfig

`GET /v1/silos/{silo_id}/signup-config` response: exactly what a signup form needs to render itself, and nothing a stranger could use to learn how the silo screens signups.

Deliberately thin relative to [`SiloSignupPolicy`] -- see that type's own doc and `system_silo_signup_policy_view`'s for the argument this record exists to satisfy without leaking the rest of the policy.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `challenge` | [SignupChallenge](schemas.md#signupchallenge) | no | A freshly issued challenge for the form to solve, present iff `challenge_mode` is [`ChallengeMode::ProofOfWork`]. `None` for [`ChallengeMode::None`] -- there is nothing to solve. |
| `challenge_mode` | [ChallengeMode](schemas.md#challengemode) | yes | Which anti-automation gate `POST .../signup` will enforce. Never [`ChallengeMode::Turnstile`], [`ChallengeMode::HCaptcha`], or [`ChallengeMode::Unknown`] on a silo this endpoint answers for at all -- `signup_enabled_for_silo` refuses those with the same 404 a disabled silo gets, so by the time this type is constructed the mode is always one this binary can both issue and verify. |
| `invite_required` | boolean | yes | Whether the form must collect an invite code. `true` is not a secret: a form that hid the field on a silo requiring one would simply fail every submission, and a stranger learns the same thing by submitting once. What stays hidden is everything about *which* codes exist -- see `SignupRequestCreate`'s own doc. Callers must keep sending a code the user supplied even when this is `false`: an open silo still redeems a valid referral code and still refuses an invalid one. |
| `payment_required` | boolean | yes | Whether the admission gate a signed-up tenant must clear requires payment ([`AdmissionRequirement::Payment`]). Reduced to a bool rather than the full [`AdmissionRequirement`] enum: a stranger's form only ever needs "will I be asked for a card", never the operator's actual admission policy. |
| `tos_version` | string | no | The terms-of-service document id the form must present. `None` when the silo's policy has not set one. |

## SignupRequestCreate

`POST /v1/silos/{silo_id}/signup` request body.

`code` is the plaintext invite code (operator-vouched or a tenant referral, see [`InviteIssuer`]). Optional, because a silo whose `invite_required` is `false` admits signups from strangers holding no code at all. Omitting it on a silo that DOES require one is refused exactly like an invalid code -- see the enumeration-resistance note below. Hashed by the handler and never logged.

Supplying a code to an open silo is not a no-op: it is validated and redeemed, so a referral is still attributed and an invalid code is still refused. A client must therefore keep sending a code the user typed even when `signup-config` reported `invite_required: false`.

`tos_version` is what the caller claims to have accepted. The server compares it against the silo's authoritative `tos_version` inside `create_signup_request`'s transaction and stores the policy's value, never this one -- the same "the server derives it, the wire value is not trusted" rule [`TenantStandingUpdate`] documents for `satisfied`. A mismatch is refused with the same indistinguishable answer every other refusal gets, so it is not a second, code-independent oracle. `None` is what a silo with no terms set expects.

`challenge_solution` is the raw JSON the ALTCHA widget posts back,

**Enumeration resistance is a property of the handler, not this type**: whether `code`+`email` redeem an invite, redeem it but for the wrong bound address, or fail for a revoked/expired/exhausted invite all answer with the identical [`SignupAccepted`] body and status. Only a *failed challenge* answers differently (400): it reveals something about the caller's own submission, never about `code` or `email`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `challenge_solution` | string | yes |  |
| `code` | string | no |  |
| `email` | string | yes |  |
| `tos_version` | string | no |  |

## SignupResendRequest

`POST /v1/silos/{silo_id}/signup/{request_id}/resend` request body.

`verification_token` is the plaintext token from the emailed link the caller currently holds -- the same value `token` carries -- and it exists here as the endpoint's ownership proof, not as a lookup key. Resend rotates the request's secret, which kills the link already in the recipient's mailbox, so an id alone must not authorize it: request ids appear in logs and audit records without their secret, and this endpoint is anonymous and internet-reachable. Compared constant-time against the stored hash inside `Store::rotate_signup_request_token`; a wrong token answers with the same [`SignupAccepted`] body as a correct one and writes nothing.

This is the first field of the fuller resend contract the design calls for (`operation_id` and a Portal-held `resend_token` alongside it). The other two depend on the Portal's pending-signup record, which does not exist yet; this one is available today because the page that offers Resend was itself loaded from the verification link.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `verification_token` | string | yes |  |

## SignupSessionIssued

`POST /v1/silos/{silo_id}/signup/{request_id}/verify` response: the one and only time a [`SignupSession`]'s plaintext token is ever on the wire.

Not [`SignupSession`] itself -- that stored record carries only `token_hash`, by design (see that type's own doc), so it has no plaintext to hand back. `session_token` is minted by the handler before the store call, hashed once for `redeem_signup_request` to store, and returned here because this response is the caller's only chance to learn it: neither `get_signup_session` nor any other read ever yields it again.

`session_id` and `session_token` together are the credential `GET .../available` and `POST .../complete` both require: presenting `session_id` alone proves nothing, since ids are not secret -- `get_signup_session`'s own doc is explicit that a caller must still check the token itself.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `email` | string | yes |  |
| `expires_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `session_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `session_token` | string | yes |  |
| `tos_version` | string | no | The terms version this signup actually accepted, as the silo's policy named it at request time. `None` when the silo had no terms set. |

## SshKey

User-supplied SSH public key, registered into one of five possible scopes (see [`SshKeyScope`]) so instance launches can pick keys to inject into authorized_keys. The User scope is the load-bearing one in practice (every user has their own personal keys); the other scopes mirror [`Image`] for symmetry and to support shared deployment keys.

The server validates the openssh wire format at create time and computes the SHA-256 fingerprint. The raw `public_key` string is stored verbatim so it can be handed to cloud-init without reformatting.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `created_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `description` | string | yes |  |
| `fingerprint` | string | yes | SHA-256 fingerprint, e.g. `SHA256:abcd...`. Server-computed at create time and stored alongside the key for cheap display / lookup. Never accepted on the wire. |
| `id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `public_key` | string | yes | OpenSSH-formatted public key — `<algo> <base64> [comment]`. Server-validated at create time; rejected with 400 if it does not parse as an OpenSSH public key. |
| `scope` | [SshKeyScope](schemas.md#sshkeyscope) | yes | Visibility scope. The variant carries the parent identity (silo_id / tenant_id / project_id / user_id) for the non-Public scopes; visibility checks resolve up the project → tenant → silo chain when needed. |

## SshKeyScope

Who an [`SshKey`] belongs to.

Two scopes only, deliberately: a key is one person's, or it is the account's. `Public`, `Silo` and `Project` were removed on 2026-08-21. An SSH key is an access credential to a running machine, so the scopes that matter are the ones a customer reasons about, and a key shared across a boundary the customer does not administer is one they cannot audit. Silo scope was the sharpest case: under D3 every self-signup account lands in one silo, so a silo-wide key would have been an access credential shared between mutually untrusted strangers.

The variant carries everything the visibility predicate needs; there are no denormalised silo_id fields on [`SshKey`]. For `Tenant`, the resolver looks up the tenant for its silo when needed. Cold path; correctness beats one extra read.

One of:

- { `kind`: `tenant`, `tenant_id`: string (uuid) }: Every member of the tenant. The account's shared key.
- { `kind`: `user`, `user_id`: string (uuid) }: One person's key.

## SshKeyScopeSelector

Owner scope selector for `GET /v1/ssh-keys?scope=...`.

One variant per collection the six pre-Wave-2 ssh-key paths served, and no more. There is no `user` variant on purpose: the caller's own keys live at `/v1/me/ssh-keys`, and offering a second spelling of that collection here is exactly what this fold exists to remove. Images do carry a `user` scope ([`ImageScopeSelector`]) because `/v1/auth/images` folds into `/v1/images` rather than surviving.

One of:

- `tenant`: Keys owned by `?tenant=`. The only selector, since an SSH key is either the tenant's or a person's, and a person reads their own through `GET /v1/auth/ssh-keys`, which binds the owner to the credential rather than trusting a `user_id` from the query. Retained as an enum rather than dropped so a future scope is an added variant instead of a reshaped query.

## Subnet

Layer-3 subnet inside a VPC. Each subnet carves a CIDR out of its parent VPC's IPv4 and/or IPv6 block. Multiple subnets may exist per VPC; their CIDRs must not overlap. NIC attach points to a specific subnet at instance-launch time.

Invariants enforced at create time: * Every present subnet CIDR must be a strict subnet of the parent VPC's same-family CIDR (`ipv4_block ⊆ vpc.ipv4_block`, `ipv6_block ⊆ vpc.ipv6_block`). * No subnet CIDR (in either family) may overlap an existing subnet CIDR in the same VPC. * At least one of `ipv4_block` / `ipv6_block` must be `Some`, and each present family must also be present on the parent VPC (an IPv4-only VPC cannot host an IPv6 subnet).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `created_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `deletion` | [SubnetDeletion](schemas.md#subnetdeletion) | no | Set while a delete of the subnet runs, and after one fails. |
| `description` | string | yes |  |
| `gateway_ipv4` | string (ipv4) | no | Upstream router on this range. A NAT gateway zone's external NIC takes it as its default route. Required when `purposes` contains `nat-gateway`. |
| `gateway_ipv6` | string (ipv6) | no |  |
| `gateway_mac` | string | no | MAC of the upstream router, set by an operator. A CN addresses outbound frames for this range to it and never learns it from the wire, where any host on the segment could answer. |
| `id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `ipv4_block` | string | no | IPv4 CIDR for this subnet. Must be a subnet of the parent VPC's `ipv4_block`, and must not overlap any other subnet's IPv4 CIDR in the same VPC. |
| `ipv6_block` | string | no | IPv6 CIDR for this subnet. Must be a subnet of the parent VPC's `ipv6_block`, and must not overlap any other subnet's IPv6 CIDR in the same VPC. |
| `kind` | [NetworkKind](schemas.md#networkkind) | no | What kind of network this subnet is. `External` subnets carry a FlatL2 nic_tag + VLAN and are the source of public / floating IPs; `Internal` / `Fabric` are VPC overlay subnets. Defaults to `Internal` for wire back-compat with pre-C-1 subnet rows. |
| `mtu` | integer (uint32) | no | Effective MTU of this range. Must not exceed the nic tag's MTU. |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `nic_tag` | string (uuid) | no | FK to the [`NicTag`] this subnet's traffic egresses on. Set for `External` subnets; `None` for overlay subnets. |
| `owner_silos` | array of string (uuid) | no | Silos allowed to allocate from this external range; empty means every silo. Always empty on a VPC subnet. |
| `platform_reserved_ipv4` | string (ipv4) | no | Address held out of NIC allocation for a platform-owned zone in this subnet (today: the SSH-broker relay, which needs a stable address so a firewall rule can name it and keep naming it across the relay's idle-reap and re-create cycle). `None` until `Store::reserve_platform_subnet_address` claims it, so a subnet that never hosts a platform zone loses nothing and every existing subnet keeps every address it has. Lives on the subnet rather than in the per-subnet NIC allocation index because instance delete clears that index; the reservation has to outlive the zone holding it. |
| `platform_reserved_ipv6` | string (ipv6) | no | IPv6 half of `platform_reserved_ipv4`. |
| `project_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `provision_end_ipv4` | string (ipv4) | no | Highest IPv4 the allocator may hand out (inclusive); `None` falls back to the block's last usable host. |
| `provision_end_ipv6` | string (ipv6) | no |  |
| `provision_start_ipv4` | string (ipv4) | no | Lowest IPv4 the allocator may hand out (inclusive); `None` falls back to the block's first usable host. Scopes a pool to a sub-range of a larger upstream block. |
| `provision_start_ipv6` | string (ipv6) | no |  |
| `purposes` | array of [AddressPurpose](schemas.md#addresspurpose) | no | Purposes this range may be allocated for, enforced when an address is allocated. An empty set is a legal declaration meaning "declared, not in service": every allocation fails. Ignored for `Internal` / `Fabric` subnets. |
| `reserved_ipv4` | array of string (ipv4) | no | Addresses inside the provision window that are never allocated: virtual router addresses, switch management addresses, anything already live on the segment. |
| `reserved_ipv6` | array of string (ipv6) | no |  |
| `resolvers` | array of string (ip) | no | Resolvers handed to a zone whose primary interface is on this range. Without this a NAT gateway zone has no DNS. |
| `route_table_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Active route table for this subnet. Defaults to the parent VPC's `main_route_table_id` at create time. |
| `ssh_relay_enabled` | boolean | no | Whether the subnet keeps an SSH relay, the platform zone that carries SSH access through the provider. When off, the relay is torn down and tunnels to the subnet are refused. |
| `tenant_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `vlan_id` | integer (uint16) | no | 802.1Q VLAN id for an `External` subnet's nic_tag link (`None` = untagged). The agent's `EnsureExternalLink` creates the matching VLAN-tagged VNIC on the nic_tag's physical link. |
| `vpc_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

## SubnetDeletion

Where a delete of a subnet stands. A subnet that is not being deleted carries none.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string | no | Why the last delete failed. |
| `since` | string (date-time) | yes | When the delete started, or when it failed. |
| `state` | [SubnetDeletionState](schemas.md#subnetdeletionstate) | yes |  |

## SubnetDeletionState

One of:

- `unknown`
- `in_progress`: The subnet's zones are being taken down; it goes when they are.
- `failed`: The delete stopped and the subnet stays. Deleting it again retries.

## TenantMemberStatus

Whether a member's account can currently sign in.

Type: `active` \| `disabled` \| `unknown`

## TenantRole

A role a tenant grants one of its members. The customer-facing vocabulary; identityd stores the grant under its own role names (`tenant_admin`, `read_only`, ...), and `identity_name` is the one place the two are tied together.

One of:

- `admin`: Everything, including members and billing.
- `member`: Create and manage the tenant's resources.
- `viewer`: Read everything, change nothing.
- `billing_viewer`: Read billing. Carries no resource access by itself.
- `billing_manager`: Read and change billing. Carries no resource access by itself.

## UpdateImageMetadata

Request body for `PUT /v1/images/{image}`.

The only mutable fields on an image are `name` and `description`. The integrity fields (`os`, `version`, `size_bytes`, `sha256`, `id`) are immutable: the id is content-addressed from `sha256` alone (scope-independent; a root import may instead preserve the upstream manifest uuid), so changing an integrity field would describe a different blob and break the reverse index that ties instances to their boot image. Owner (`scope`) is changed via the owner endpoint, not here.

Both fields are optional. Omitting a field leaves it unchanged (a no-op edit with both fields `None` returns the image as-is). A `name` change re-points the per-scope name index atomically and rejects (409) a collision with an existing image in the same scope.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | string | no | New description. `None` leaves the description unchanged; pass `Some("")` to clear it. |
| `name` | string | no | New display name. Must be free among images in the same scope. `None` leaves the name unchanged. |

## UsernameAvailability

`GET /v1/silos/{silo_id}/signup/{request_id}/available?username=...` response.

Reachable only from inside a redeemed, still-live session -- see `signup_username_probe`'s own doc for the gate. `available` alone, nothing about why a taken name is taken: this binary's own `get_user_by_username` uniqueness is cluster-wide operator/legacy tenant-user accounts, not the eventual identityd-federated realm a completed signup actually lands in, so this is a best-effort, pre-`/complete` preview rather than a guarantee.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `available` | boolean | yes |  |

## Vpc

Tenant VPC. Project-scoped, tenant-rooted. Mirrors the per-VPC fields OPTE consumes in `oxide_vpc::api::VpcCfg`: a 24-bit Geneve VNI plus an optional primary IPv4 CIDR and optional primary IPv6 CIDR (matching OPTE's `IpCfg` enum: Ipv4-only, Ipv6-only, or dual-stack). Per-NIC concerns (guest MAC, private IPs, external IPs, attached_subnets, DHCP) are *not* on the VPC record — those land on subnet/instance/NIC resources in later slices.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `created_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `description` | string | yes |  |
| `id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `ipv4_block` | string | no | Primary IPv4 CIDR for the VPC overlay. `None` for IPv6-only. Wire format is the canonical CIDR string, e.g. `"10.0.0.0/24"`. |
| `ipv6_block` | string | no | Primary IPv6 CIDR for the VPC overlay. `None` for IPv4-only. Wire format is the canonical CIDR string, e.g. `"fd00::/48"`. |
| `main_route_table_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Route table inherited by new subnets unless explicitly reassociated later. Created atomically with the VPC. |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `project_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `tenant_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `vni` | integer (uint32) | yes | Geneve Virtual Network Identifier. Server-assigned at create time, drawn from `[VPC_VNI_RESERVED_CEILING, VPC_VNI_MAX)`, unique rack-wide. |
